mode: lighter refresh (UNCHANGED this run; interaction-context only)
summary: Deployed SINGLE-token nudge batch minter. `batchMint` mints `count` NFTs to `recipient` via the trusted owner-pinned tokenMinter, pulling the derived payment token upfront and refunding surplus; when count>=nudgeSize it pays `recipient` this contract's pre-loop balance of the single `nudgePaymentToken` ('donate forward'). This is the story-022 sibling that the multi-token nudge was split OUT of; it has a single owner-set reward token (not a whitelist array) and is NOT ReentrancyGuard (no caller-supplied token addresses to call). Unchanged this run.

verifiedProperties.noUnboundedLoops: batchMint mint loop bounded by caller-paid `count` (caller funds the gas/payment); single-token payout, no reward array
verifiedProperties.reentrancyGuarded: NONE — deliberately not ReentrancyGuard. Rationale: the only external token calls are the trusted, owner-set nudgePaymentToken and tokenMinter; no caller-supplied address is invoked (contrast BatchNFTMinterMultiToken, which IS guarded because whitelisted tokens execute arbitrary code).

carriedForwardNotes: Winner-take-all / front-runnable nudge payout is the known accepted design (run-21: NFTs carry no redemption value; pot < nudgeSize mint cost; every claim net-positive). Not a new finding.
Reward snapshot is read PRE-loop and paid POST-loop ('donate forward') — same load-bearing mechanic as the multi-token variant; do not move the balance read to the payout site.

externalEntryPoints.notes: NOT nonReentrant — single trusted reward token

trustAssumptions: tokenMinter and dispatcher trusted/owner-pinned; nudgePaymentToken owner-set and standard ERC20.
Nudge economics intentionally winner-take-all; over-funding beyond mint cost is a sender error (accepted).
No reentrancy guard is safe ONLY because no caller-supplied token address is ever called — a property the multi-token variant does not share.
